text:
aria: heads up — private cluster pvt-7 seeing a 99th percentile latency spike for model-unify starting ~03:40 UTC. Throughput down ~20%. graphs: https://graf.redwood/pvt-7/model-unify
sam: saw the alert, digging into traces. early signal looks like lots of 502s from egress NAT
miguel: pulling nat gateway logs now, conntrack rejects are spiking
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-487 — pvt-7 egress latency spike
sam: flamegraphs show the path fell back to a generic fragment handler in the kernel -> higher tail latency
tess: kv-cache miss rate jumped ~4.3x at the same time. batching heuristics rollout yesterday at 02:50? @sam @kai
kai: confirmed — shipped a small batching threshold tweak (min_batch_seconds 0.004 -> 0.002) to reduce perceived latency for tiny prompts
aria: hypothesis: more, smaller outbound flows from runtime may be increasing conntrack churn and SNAT port use. plausible?
miguel: nat logs snippet:
```
Mar 12 03:41:12 nat-gw kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Mar 12 03:41:13 nat-gw kernel: nf_conntrack: quota exceeded
```
miguel: also seeing a storm of short-lived source ports from a single host 10.100.9.21
sam: that host is the new customer-runner service — looks like a noisy neighbor spawning many ephemeral sockets concurrently
tess: quick mitigations we can try now:
- bump net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
- clamp MTU on egress to avoid fragmentation-related slow paths
- reserve an SNAT port pool for critical services
- rollback the batching tweak if it proves causal
aria: i'll request rollback. @ops-bot can you start rollback of the runtime change?
ops-bot: rollback job queued (job id rbd-778). starting canary revert on pvt-7
kai: i'll open a batching PR to make the floor adaptive based on conntrack pressure and request shape
miguel: applied conntrack_max bump (400k -> 1M) on nat-gw and added a small SNAT port reserve for pvt-7 services
sam: rolled back batching change on canary nodes — seeing immediate improvement and reduced KV miss amplification
tess: patched firewall to DROP INVALID fragments and added MTU clamp 1400 on the egress path
infra-bot: alert resolved: latency returned to baseline
aria: good, 99th returned to normal. we still see short KV thrash on a few hot keys — likely cache key variation introduced by batching changes
kai: note — the batching change altered request shapes; cache key included raw chunk order. i'll normalize cache-key generation to be order-insensitive for small prompts
aria: action items: postmortem + runbook for conntrack pressure on private NATs. i've started a doc: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/INC-2026-487
sam: adding perf profile + KV eviction graphs to the postmortem
tess: thanks all :thumbsup:
